en: to slow down or block progress
ex: Heavy snow impeded the rescue efforts.

en: to make something difficult to do
ex: Poor lighting hindered the researchers' observations.

en: to prevent someone from succeeding
ex: Quick action by the guards thwarted the robbery.

en: to prevent progress; to block
ex: A lack of funding stymied the project for two years.

en: to slow down or restrict movement or progress
ex: Strong winds hampered efforts to put out the fire.

en: to restrain or slow down a process
ex: Cold temperatures inhibit the growth of bacteria.

en: to prove that a statement is false
ex: The scientist refuted the claim with clear experimental data.

en: to argue that a claim is false
ex: The lawyer rebutted each point the prosecution made.

en: to dispute or challenge something
ex: Several historians contest the traditional date of the battle.

en: to openly refuse to obey
ex: The young activists defied the ban and gathered in the square.

en: to refuse to accept or be associated with something
ex: The party repudiated the candidate's offensive remarks.

en: to give up control or a claim voluntarily
ex: The founder finally relinquished control of the company to her son.

en: to choose to go without something
ex: Many students forgo summer vacations to take extra classes.

en: to formally give up a claim, belief, or title
ex: He renounced his title and moved abroad.

en: to abandon someone or something
ex: She refused to forsake her friends when they needed her.

en: to choose not to require or use a right
ex: The museum waives the entry fee on the first Sunday of every month.

en: to examine something very carefully
ex: The editor scrutinized every figure in the report.

en: to investigate something thoroughly
ex: Journalists probed the company's financial records.

en: to assess the value or quality of something
ex: An expert appraised the old painting at twice the expected price.

en: to estimate or judge something
ex: The survey was designed to gauge public opinion on the new park.

en: to expect or predict something
ex: The organizers anticipated a large crowd and added more chairs.

en: to know about something before it happens
ex: Few economists foresaw the crisis.

en: to be a sign that something, usually bad, will happen
ex: Dark clouds portended a violent storm.

en: to be a warning sign of a future event
ex: The early frost presaged a long, hard winter.

en: to try to match or surpass someone admired
ex: Young players often emulate their favorite athletes.

en: to copy someone's actions, voice, or appearance
ex: Some insects mimic the color of leaves to avoid predators.

en: to repeat an experiment or result exactly
ex: Other laboratories failed to replicate the surprising results.

en: to take the place of something
ex: Streaming services have largely supplanted DVDs.

en: to replace something older or less effective
ex: The new rules supersede all previous guidelines.

en: to make something seem less important by comparison
ex: Her second album eclipsed the success of her first.

en: to agree with an opinion
ex: Most experts concur that regular exercise improves mood.

en: to accept something reluctantly without protest
ex: After hours of debate, the manager acquiesced to the workers' demands.

en: to act according to a rule or request
ex: All new buildings must comply with the safety code.

uz: goh u, goh bu fikrga o'tmoq
en: to keep changing one's mind
ex: He vacillated between studying medicine and studying law.

en: to become unsure or weaker in a decision
ex: Her support for the plan never wavered.

en: to lose strength or momentum; to hesitate
ex: The economy faltered after the factory closed.

en: to depart from the usual course or plan
ex: The pilot deviated from the planned route to avoid a storm.

en: to move away from the main subject in speech or writing
ex: The lecturer often digressed into stories about his childhood.

en: to separate and go in different directions
ex: The two scientists' views diverged on the cause of the disease.

en: to make full use of; or to use unfairly
ex: The company exploited a gap in the market for cheap, durable phones.

en: to control and use a natural force or resource
ex: Engineers harness the river's energy to produce electricity.

en: to use something to maximum advantage
ex: The startup leveraged its social media following to raise funds.

en: to find a way around a rule or obstacle
ex: Some drivers circumvent the toll by taking back roads.

en: to escape or avoid, often by trickery
ex: The senator evaded the reporter's question about the budget.

en: to deliberately avoid using or doing something
ex: The chef eschews frozen ingredients.

en: to persistently avoid someone or something
ex: After the scandal, many former friends shunned him.

en: to emphasize the importance of something
ex: The flood underscored the need for better drainage.

en: to make something more noticeable
ex: The bright frame accentuates the colors in the painting.

en: to make secret or new information known
ex: The company refused to disclose how much it paid for the land.

en: to reveal private or secret information
ex: Journalists must never divulge their sources.

uz: ilk bor taqdim etmoq, pardani ochmoq
en: to show or announce something publicly for the first time
ex: The city unveiled its plan for a new metro line.

en: to pay no attention to something
ex: Many drivers disregard the speed limit on this road.

en: to fail to notice or consider something
ex: The report overlooks the cost of maintaining the new bridge.

en: to make someone less angry
ex: The airline offered free meals to placate the delayed passengers.

en: to calm someone by giving them what they want
ex: The government lowered fuel prices to appease protesters.

en: to make an unpleasant feeling less intense
ex: The doctor's explanation assuaged the patient's fears.

en: to confuse someone completely
ex: The strange results perplexed the research team.

en: to surprise or confuse, especially by acting against expectations
ex: The young team confounded the critics by winning the title.

en: to continue firmly despite difficulty
ex: Despite many failures, the inventor persisted.

uz: davom ettirib, saqlab qolmoq (ko'pincha yomon narsani)
en: to make a situation, often a bad one, continue
ex: Such jokes perpetuate harmful stereotypes.

en: to keep something going over time
ex: The runner could not sustain her pace in the final lap.

en: to give a share of something for a particular purpose
ex: Each student is allotted ten minutes to present.

en: to spread information widely
ex: The health ministry disseminated the guidelines through schools.

en: to take in and fully understand information or ideas
ex: It takes time to assimilate so much new vocabulary.

en: to combine different ideas into a connected whole
ex: The review synthesizes the findings of forty studies.

en: to make two different ideas or people agree
ex: It is hard to reconcile the company's green image with its pollution record.

uz: ko'z yummoq, jim turib yo'l qo'ymoq
en: to accept behavior that is considered wrong
ex: The school does not condone cheating of any kind.
